Gravity causes planets to be pulled into a roughly spherical shape, so a planet's size can be expressed roughly by an average radius (for example, [Earth radius](/wiki/Earth_radius_(unit) "Earth radius (unit)") or [Jupiter radius](/wiki/Jupiter_radius "Jupiter radius")). However, planets are not perfectly spherical; for example, the [Earth's rotation](/wiki/Earth%27s_rotation "Earth's rotation") causes it to be slightly flattened at the poles with a [bulge around the equator](/wiki/Equatorial_bulge "Equatorial bulge").[[96]](#cite_note-milbert_smith96-97) Therefore, a better approximation of Earth's shape is an [oblate spheroid](/wiki/Oblate_spheroid "Oblate spheroid"), whose equatorial diameter is 43 kilometers (27 mi) larger than the [pole](/wiki/Geographical_pole "Geographical pole")-to-pole diameter.[[97]](#cite_note-ngdc2006-98) Generally, a planet's shape may be described by giving polar and equatorial radii of a [spheroid](/wiki/Spheroid "Spheroid") or specifying a [reference ellipsoid](/wiki/Reference_ellipsoid "Reference ellipsoid"). From such a specification, the planet's flattening, surface area, and volume can be calculated; its [normal gravity](/wiki/Normal_gravity "Normal gravity") can be computed knowing its size, shape, rotation rate, and mass.[[98]](#cite_note-99)

Essential amino acid :: Interchangeability :: chunk_0011
The distinction between essential and non-essential amino acids is somewhat unclear, as some amino acids can be produced from others. The [sulfur](/wiki/Sulfur "Sulfur")-containing amino acids, [methionine](/wiki/Methionine "Methionine") and [homocysteine](/wiki/Homocysteine "Homocysteine"), can be converted into each other but neither can be synthesized *de novo* in humans. Likewise, cysteine can be made from homocysteine but cannot be synthesized on its own. So, for convenience, sulfur-containing amino acids are sometimes considered a single pool of nutritionally equivalent amino acids as are the [aromatic](/wiki/Aromatic "Aromatic") amino acid pair, [phenylalanine](/wiki/Phenylalanine "Phenylalanine") and [tyrosine](/wiki/Tyrosine "Tyrosine"). Likewise [arginine](/wiki/Arginine "Arginine"), [ornithine](/wiki/Ornithine "Ornithine"), and [citrulline](/wiki/Citrulline "Citrulline"), which are interconvertible by the [urea cycle](/wiki/Urea_cycle "Urea cycle"), are considered a single group.

At age sixteen, Adams entered [Harvard College](/wiki/Harvard_College "Harvard College") in 1751, studying under [Joseph Mayhew](/wiki/Joseph_Mayhew "Joseph Mayhew").[[10]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMcCullough200135-12) As an adult, Adams was a keen scholar, studying the works of ancient writers such as [Thucydides](/wiki/Thucydides "Thucydides"), [Plato](/wiki/Plato "Plato"), [Cicero](/wiki/Cicero "Cicero"), and [Tacitus](/wiki/Tacitus "Tacitus") in their original languages.[[11]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMcCullough200113-13) Though his father expected him to be a minister,[[12]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFerling199216-14) after his 1755 graduation with an [A.B. degree](/wiki/Bachelor_of_Arts "Bachelor of Arts"), he taught school temporarily in [Worcester](/wiki/Worcester,_Massachusetts "Worcester, Massachusetts"), while pondering his permanent vocation. In the next four years, he began to seek prestige, craving "Honour or Reputation" and "more defference from [his] fellows", and was determined to be "a great Man". He decided to become a lawyer, writing his father that he found among lawyers "noble and gallant achievements" but, among the clergy, the "pretended sanctity of some absolute dunces". He had reservations about his self-described "trumpery" and failure to share the "happiness of [his] fellow men".[[13]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFerling199217–18-15)

When the [French and Indian War](/wiki/French_and_Indian_War "French and Indian War") began in 1754, Adams, aged nineteen, felt guilty he was the first in his family not to be a militia officer; he said "I longed more ardently to be a Soldier than I ever did to be a Lawyer".[[14]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFerling199221-16)

Shoko Ieiri (家入 硝子, *Ieiri Shoko*) is a Jujutsu Sorcerer doctor at Tokyo Prefectural Jujutsu High School and former classmate of Satoru Gojo and Suguru Geto. She has proven to be quite a valuable resource, being one of the few people capable of healing others with the Reverse Cursed Technique (反転 術式, *Hanten Jutsushiki*). Shoko is a rather serious and somber person, wants nothing more than to get her job done, although she shares a long-standing friendship with fellow sorcerers Gojo and Utahime. Unlike the other sorcerers, she does not engage in combat. She usually examines dead bodies in the school morgue, since her ability to output positive energy is considered too valuable and rare to risk on dangerous missions. After Ijichi and Ino are severely injured by Curse Users in Shibuya, she saves their lives, as well as Megumi's following his bout with Shigemo. During the Shinjuku Showdown, she heals many of the combatants injured by Sukuna, with Arata and Amai's help. She also helps Yuta transplant his brain into Gojo's corpse with Kenjaku's technique.

Europe lies mainly in the [temperate](/wiki/Temperate "Temperate") climate zone of the northern hemisphere, where the [prevailing wind direction is from the west](/wiki/Prevailing_westerlies "Prevailing westerlies"). The climate is milder in comparison to other areas of the same latitude around the globe due to the influence of the [Gulf Stream](/wiki/Gulf_Stream "Gulf Stream"), an ocean current which carries warm water from the [Gulf of Mexico](/wiki/Gulf_of_Mexico "Gulf of Mexico") across the [Atlantic Ocean](/wiki/Atlantic_Ocean "Atlantic Ocean") to Europe.[[238]](#cite_note-climate-238) The Gulf Stream is nicknamed "Europe's central heating", because it makes Europe's climate warmer and wetter than it would otherwise be. The Gulf Stream not only carries warm water to Europe's coast but also warms up the prevailing westerly winds that blow across the continent from the Atlantic Ocean.

This is a **list of countries by coffee production**, based on data from the [Food and Agriculture Organization](/wiki/Food_and_Agriculture_Organization "Food and Agriculture Organization") (FAO) for 2023. This data covers the production of [green coffee beans](/wiki/Green_coffee_bean "Green coffee bean"), the primary ingredient in the production of processed coffee. Roasting and packaging of [ground coffee](/wiki/Ground_coffee "Ground coffee") often takes place after it has been exported from the producing nation; see the separate [list of countries by coffee exports](/wiki/List_of_countries_by_coffee_exports "List of countries by coffee exports").

Coffee is a [cash crop](/wiki/Cash_crop "Cash crop") in many areas, with the amount produced for export significantly in excess of local demand. [Springfield, Missouri](/wiki/Springfield,_Missouri "Springfield, Missouri"), has hosted professional baseball teams since as early as 1905, when the Springfield Highlanders began play. For nearly 30 years, the team was variously called the Highlanders, Jobbers, Midgets, and Merchants. There were several years when no team existed at all.

In 1931, the St. Louis Cardinals purchased a minor league team, renamed it the Cardinals, and relocated it in Springfield. That year, the team won the first of several [Western Association](/wiki/Western_Association "Western Association") titles. With a front office led by future [Hall of Famer](/wiki/Baseball_Hall_of_Fame "Baseball Hall of Fame") [Branch Rickey](/wiki/Branch_Rickey "Branch Rickey"), Springfield also went to the playoffs in 1931, 1932, 1934, 1935, 1937, 1938, 1939, and 1941, and won league titles in 1931, 1932, 1934, 1937, and 1939.

Following the 1946 season, St. Louis moved the team to [St. Joseph, Missouri](/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri "St. Joseph, Missouri"), where it remained until 1953. The city of Springfield saw a brief re-emergence of minor league baseball when the rival [Chicago Cubs](/wiki/Chicago_Cubs "Chicago Cubs") moved its affiliate to Springfield for one season taking the name Springfield Cubs.

Though there was a gap of 63 years, most in the Springfield and St. Louis organizations consider the current Cardinals the same group which existed in 1932. Many pieces of fan apparel actually say "Springfield Cardinals circa 1932." The deck on top of the Cardinals dugout also has the championship banners from the 1930s and 1940s.

2. **[^](#cite_ref-HonoluluHI_2-0)** The [State of Hawaiʻi](/wiki/Hawaii "Hawaii") has no incorporated municipalities other than the [City and County of Honolulu](/wiki/Honolulu_County,_Hawaii "Honolulu County, Hawaii"), which comprises the entire [Island of Oʻahu](/wiki/Oahu "Oahu"). In accordance with Hawaiian law, the [United States Census Bureau](/wiki/United_States_Census_Bureau "United States Census Bureau") defines the state's cities and towns as [Census Designated Places](/wiki/Census-designated_place "Census-designated place") (CDPs). The Census Bureau defines the [Urban Honolulu CDP](/wiki/Honolulu,_Hawaii "Honolulu, Hawaii") as the portion of the City and County of Honolulu that is coextensive with the Judicial District of Honolulu. The Urban Honolulu CDP is what is generally thought of as the "city" of [Honolulu](/wiki/Honolulu "Honolulu"), and its population is used here and in other population comparisons. The Urban Honolulu CDP is currently the most populous Census Designated Place in the United States. The [Honolulu, HI Metropolitan Statistical Area](/wiki/Honolulu,_HI_Metropolitan_Statistical_Area "Honolulu, HI Metropolitan Statistical Area") comprises the entire City and County of Honolulu.
